cause: Charge-only USB cable, or a browser other than Chrome / Edge
fix: Try another cable and use Chrome. Close other tabs or apps using the serial port.

symptom: Board not found even after changing the cable
cause: MicroPython firmware missing or the wrong firmware
fix: Hold BOOTSEL while plugging in, then flash the Raspberry Pi Pico W MicroPython firmware (not the plain Pico one).

symptom: "Device busy" or the serial monitor stays empty
cause: Another tab or program has the port open
fix: Close other MicroLab or serial tabs, unplug for 5 seconds, reconnect.

symptom: Onboard LED doesn't blink with Pin(25)
cause: On the Pico W the LED is on the Wi-Fi chip
Typo, missing colon or wrong indentation
fix: Read the line number in the error, then read that line aloud together.

cause: Library file not on the board
fix: Upload the .py library files with the MicroLab file manager, then run again.

symptom: Light readings: Dark and Bright are swapped
cause: Code copied from the internet, where the LDR is wired the other way
fix: On MakerPy, more light = higher number. Check DARK is the smaller threshold.

cause: LM35 is powered from 3.3 V on this board
fix: Compare with a thermometer and add an offset in code if needed.

cause: STBY is LOW or the 9 V adapter isn't plugged in
fix: Set Pin(14) HIGH and plug in the 9 V adapter.

cause: IN1 and IN2 swapped in code, or motor wires reversed
fix: AIN1 = GPIO 13, AIN2 = GPIO 12, BIN1 = GPIO 17, BIN2 = GPIO 16. Or swap that motor's two wires.

symptom: LCD lights up but shows nothing
cause: Contrast not set, or wrong I2C address
fix: Turn the small blue contrast screw on the backpack. Run an I2C scan; the address is usually 0x27 or 0x3F.

symptom: HC-SR04 always reads 0 or a huge number
cause: Trig and Echo swapped, or the divider is wired wrong
fix: Trig → GPIO 21, Echo → divider → GPIO 22. Check GND is shared.
